correctness.rationale: Four or more whites preclude any first force since a blue vertex misses at most two whites in the path complement. For exactly three whites, a first force exists precisely when they include a pair a,a+2 about a blue center. After it, one of a−1,a+3 exists and can force one of the last two whites, and the complement has positive minimum degree for the final force. Counting witnesses and subtracting the n−4 double-witness triples gives (n−3)²+1. Every transition has a unique common white pair, so the completion-set binomial counts are disjoint. To replay the grouped counts for separation d≥3, write k=n−d: the two inward labels are always present and coincide only for d=4; each outward label occurs in max(0,k−2) completions sets indexed by the shared pair, and both occur jointly in max(0,k−4). Thus the unrestricted group count is k+4max(0,k−2)+max(0,k−4) for d=3 or d≥5 and 2max(0,k−2)+max(0,k−4) for d=4. Together with d=1 and 2 in the completion table this reproduces the unrestricted cubic. Consecutive completions at d=2 survive in the two intervals outside the three omitted labels; d=3 and 5 each give one consecutive pair per shared pair, with no other losses, yielding n²−5n+4 prohibited moves. For n≥7, connected fibres follow because a disconnected complement of an induced linear forest with at least four vertices would give a star with three leaves or a K₂,₂ cut. Overlap links each parity; 023↔035 joins them. At n=6 the isolated positions of the two endpoint fibres are absorbed by the overlapping connected fibres. At n=5 the unrestricted cycle is 013–023–024–124–134–013 and only 134↔013 is a slide. A separate finite enumeration using single forces and all state pairs for n=5 through 14 agreed in counts and slide component sizes, including (21 exchanges, 11 slides) at n=6. The all-order replay is RESULT.md Lemmas 1–3; the supplied scripts were inspected but not executed, and finite enumeration alone is not the proof.

evidence: Geneson et al. treat exchanges in base paths/cycles and connectivity for forests; path complements at the orders in question are not forests. Curl et al. give Z(overline T)=n−3 for complements of nonstar trees. The cycle-complement record gives slide connectivity for n≥7 and disconnectedness at n=6.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The scalar nonstar-tree theorem covers the old minimum. The cycle-complement result is for a different state space: deleting the cycle's wraparound edge in the original graph changes both witness triples and the allowed slides in the complement. In particular its n=6 slide graph is disconnected and the path complement's is connected. The generic forest or base path/cycle results do not subsume this case.

value.rationale: Minimum-state reachability by graph-local moves is a natural question in zero-forcing reconfiguration. Three isolated optimum states at n=5 become part of a single connected space from n=6 onward even though the unrestricted graph is already connected at n=5. The fibre proof gives usable reachability structure. The exact edge formulas independently quantify the loss from restricting moves: quadratic lost edges out of cubic exchange edges, rather than just an unquantified connectivity comparison. These results go beyond reproducing a known minimum-set count.
